What this PR does / why we need it:
Add MLA to SGLangLayerwise.
Special notes for your reviewers:
Also add unit test code in tests/v1/test_gpu_connector.py and passed it.
Unit test command:

pytest tests/v1/test_gpu_connector.py::test_batched_layerwise_sglang_connector_with_gpu_and_mla -v
  • this PR contains unit tests

Note

Medium Risk
Touches CUDA KV-transfer kernels and the Python/C++ binding API for SGLang KV movement, so mistakes could corrupt KV buffers or cause subtle runtime crashes. Scope is contained to SGLang layerwise/offload paths and is covered by a new parametric unit test.

Overview
Adds MLA support for SGLang layerwise KV offload/load by teaching the SGLang single-layer transfer path to operate on a single KV buffer (no separate value cache) and by plumbing gpu_kv_format through single_layer_kv_transfer_sgl.

This updates the CUDA kernel and C++/pybind signature to accept sgl_key_value_cache as a vector of tensors, conditionally skipping value transfers for MLA, and adjusts SGLang connectors/adapters to allow v_pool=None and to set/validate MemoryFormat.KV_MLA_FMT where appropriate.

Also simplifies the SGLang integration README install instructions and adds a new pytest covering SGLangLayerwiseGPUConnector for both use_gpu and use_mla.

Summary of Changes

Hello @huangzhengxiang, I'm Gemini Code Assist1! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed!

This pull request significantly enhances the SGLangLayerwise GPU connector by integrating Multi-Layer Attention (MLA) capabilities. The changes involve introducing specialized CUDA kernels and adapting the Python-side logic to efficiently manage and transfer KV caches when MLA is active. This ensures that the system can correctly handle both standard and MLA-formatted memory, improving flexibility and performance for models utilizing MLA.

Highlights

  • MLA Support in SGLangLayerwise: Introduced Multi-Layer Attention (MLA) support within the SGLangLayerwise GPU connector, enabling specialized handling of KV caches for MLA configurations.
  • CUDA Kernel Enhancements: Modified the single_layer_kv_transfer_sgl_kernel to be templated with a USE_MLA flag and added a new single_layer_kv_transfer_sgl_mla function for MLA-specific KV cache transfers.
  • Python Binding Updates: Exposed the new single_layer_kv_transfer_sgl_mla function to Python through pybind.cpp.
  • GPU Connector Logic: Updated SGLangLayerwiseGPUConnector to conditionally use MLA-specific logic for memory format validation, KV cache transfers, and shape determination.
  • Unit Testing: Added a new unit test, test_batched_layerwise_sglang_connector_with_gpu_and_mla, to thoroughly validate the MLA functionality across different GPU and MLA configurations.
  • Documentation Update: Simplified the SGLang installation instructions in the README.md for integration examples.

Code Review

This pull request introduces MLA (Multi-Layer Attention) support to SGLangLayerwise by modifying several core files, updating the SGLangLayerwiseGPUConnector, and adding a new unit test. However, a critical vulnerability has been identified: the implementation lacks sufficient validation of the slot_mapping tensor, which could lead to out-of-bounds memory access on the GPU. Additionally, there are potential division-by-zero scenarios in the CUDA kernels that could be exploited for denial-of-service attacks. Addressing these security concerns is crucial before merging.

Repeated _lazy_initialize_buffer calls crash on reshaped tensors

High Severity

_lazy_initialize_buffer permanently reshapes kvcache tensors from 3D to 4D via .view() but has no guard preventing re-execution. On a second request, format-discovery helpers like get_head_size and get_num_heads read wrong dimensions from the already-reshaped 4D tensors (e.g., for MLA, get_head_size returns shape[2]=1 instead of the actual head size). The resulting kv_shape is incorrect, and the subsequent .view() crashes because element counts don't match. The previous code avoided this by creating temporary views inline at each kernel call site rather than mutating the list.

Additional Locations (2)
  • lmcache/v1/gpu_connector/gpu_connectors.py#L1734-L1735
  • lmcache/v1/gpu_connector/gpu_connectors.py#L1883-L1884

In the current code _lazy_initialize_buffer only performs format discovery/allocation under self.gpu_buffer_allocator is None and the 4D .view(...) calls are temporary at transfer sites, so tensors are not permanently reshaped across requests.
